ai.title: Fix navigation error on referral redemption page
ai.summary: Referral pages now handle fetch errors gracefully instead of crashing on back navigation. `web/src/app/referrals/[code]/page.tsx` and `web/src/app/referrals/page.tsx` update `useQuery` to throw on `!res.ok` and render `CardWithBeams` for errors. Query keys include `params.code` to prevent cache collisions. Removed unused `redirect` import from `web/src/app/layout.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you visit a referral page and the site can't load the referral details, the page now shows a friendly error message instead of crashing, especially if you hit the back button. This affects anyone trying to view or redeem referral links. You would notice that the page no longer breaks unexpectedly and instead clearly tells you something went wrong, like 'We couldn't fetch your referral data.' The fix is live today.

ai.title: Fix Twitch message processing loop
ai.summary: Moved `break` statement in `npm-app/twitch-plays-codebuff.sh` outside the conditional check. Ensures loop termination after processing the first valid message, preventing unnecessary iteration. Updated `npm-app/knowledge.md` with rules for historical message processing.

eli5.text: The Twitch chat processing system was stuck in a loop where it kept checking for new messages instead of stopping after finding the first valid one. Now it correctly stops after processing the first real message, so it doesn't waste time re-reading old messages. You probably didn't notice anything wrong, but behind the scenes this makes the system more efficient and prevents duplicate or out-of-order messages from being processed.

ai.title: Twitch polling interval 15s and command prefix
ai.summary: Polling interval reduced from 60s to 15s in `npm-app/twitch-plays-codebuff.sh`. Filter logic now requires `>` prefix for commands and processes last 10 messages. Deduplication via `last_message` prevents re-sending.

eli5.text: If you're in Twitch chat, your messages now reach the game roughly four times faster, the system checks chat every 15 seconds instead of waiting a full minute. Commands must now be prefixed with a greater-than sign (like ">forward"), and only messages starting that way will be acted on, which keeps regular chat chatter from accidentally controlling the game. The system also remembers the last message it acted on, so it won't trigger the same command twice. These changes affect anyone sending commands to the Codebuff game on Twitch.
